steps.title: Saying what you prefer
steps.html:
FormExample
prefer + nounI prefer the map.
prefer + -ingI prefer walking to driving.
would prefer to + verbI'd prefer to take the GPS.
would rather + verb (no to)I'd rather take the GPS.
Comparing twoI'd rather take the map than the GPS.

I'd is the short form of I would. It is what people actually say.

would rather never takes to: I'd rather stay, not I'd rather to stay.

steps.title: Giving a reason
steps.html:
WordOrderExample
becauseresult, then reasonWe can cook inside because we have the stove.
soreason, then resultWe have the stove, so we can cook inside.

because answers why? so gives the result.

The two halves swap places: what follows because comes before so.
